intro_html: Meatloaf gets mocked, and meatloaf does not care. It is one of the few dinners that actually improves after a night in the fridge, and it slices to weight better than almost anything else you can cook. This one is turkey, bound with egg and bread crumbs, glazed with ketchup and barbecue sauce, served over rice. Each serving comes to 599 calories with 32 grams of protein for about $2.92 (at everyday cost), and a genuinely cheap plate.
cost_closing_html: About $2.92 a serving (at everyday cost). Bread crumbs and egg stretch the turkey without watering down the protein, which is the entire reason meatloaf became a Depression-era staple in the first place.
shop_smart: Ground turkey in the largest pack you can freeze is the single biggest lever on this recipe's price. Everything else in the pan costs pennies by comparison.
Bread crumbs are the item people overpay for the most. A canister lasts many batches, and stale sandwich bread run through a food processor is free.
Ketchup, barbecue sauce, Worcestershire, and Dijon are all shelf-stable for a year or more. Buy the store-brand bottles once and they will carry you through a dozen recipes.
Rice bought in the big bag is the cheapest starch in the store per serving. There is no such thing as rice going bad on you before you use it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the diced onion and green bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for one minute and let the mixture cool. Hot vegetables will start cooking the egg.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs with the heavy cream, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and black pepper, then stir in the bread crumbs and let them soak for 5 minutes.
Add the ground turkey, the cooled vegetables, and the shredded cheddar. Mix with your hands only until it comes together. Overworking meatloaf turns it dense and rubbery.
Divide the mixture between three loaf pans or shape it into three free-form loaves on a sheet pan. Smaller loaves cook faster and slice more evenly than one giant brick.
Stir the ketchup and barbecue sauce together and brush half of it over the loaves, then bake at 350F for 45 to 55 minutes until the centers read 165F.
Brush on the rest of the glaze and return the loaves for 10 minutes so it sets into a lacquer instead of running off.
Cook the rice while the loaves rest at least 15 minutes, then slice the meatloaf and portion it over the rice.
portion_html: Weigh the rice and the sliced meatloaf together, subtract your empty pot weight, and divide by 14. Meatloaf slices look identical and weigh nothing alike, so let the scale settle it. Every serving comes to 599 calories and 32 grams of protein.

head.description: Turkey meatloaf meal prep with a ketchup and BBQ glaze, served over rice. 599 calories, 32g protein, about $2.92 a serving (at everyday cost) across 14 containers.
head.keywords: turkey meatloaf, ground turkey meal prep, budget dinner, meatloaf and mashed potatoes, high protein meal prep, cheap family dinner
steps: Cook the onion, bell pepper, and garlic in butter until soft, then cool.
Whisk the eggs with cream, Dijon, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper, stir in the bread crumbs, and soak 5 minutes.
Mix in the ground turkey, cooled vegetables, and cheddar by hand, then shape into three loaves.
Glaze with half the ketchup and BBQ mixture and bake at 350F for 45 to 55 minutes to 165F, then glaze again and bake 10 minutes more.
Cook the rice, rest the loaves 15 minutes, slice, and portion over rice into 14 containers.
